newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares close higher on bargain-buying.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares close higher on bargain-buying.

text.p: The Lima bolsa made light gains Wednesday as investors took cautious advantage of lower prices following Tuesday's drastic drop on internal political problems, brokers said.
Analysts expected the market to show the same tendency Thursday as the attractiveness of low share prices was seen likely to narrowly outweigh political worries.
According to preliminary figures, the Lima Stock Exchange's general index rose 1.01 percent to 2,123.01 points, while the blue-chip selective index rose 0.43 percent to 3,045.18 points.
The total amount traded was 50 million soles ($19 million) in 2,324 transactions. Overall, 43 shares rose, 17 dropped and 21 remained stable.

"Despite purchases to take advantage of the lower prices after Tuesday's fall, there is a note of fear in the acquisitions," said Edgar Saravia from Latinoamericana brokerage. "I believe that the way things stand, the best thing is to remain cautious."

The bolsa dropped 5.64 percent Tuesday because of a fall in the Brazilian market, and a political storm in Peru over allegations that secret services were tapping phone conversations and the revocation of local citizenship from Israeli-born TV station owner Baruch Ivcher.

"The market also felt the possibility of a (currency) devaluation in Brazil," said Carlos Ugaz from Finvest brokerage. "But it would only have been felt lightly had it not been for the political risk."

Market sources said that investors are currently relying on companies having good financial reports from the first half, and also on the presidential address scheduled for July 28 which they hope will reduce tensions.
"The recovery of the economy cannot be denied, and it is a factor that can push up many sectors, especially mining and brewery stocks," said Saravia.

Winners today included Banco de Credito with 3.31 percent to 3.74 soles, brewer Union de Cervecerias Backus with 3.08 percent to 2.34 soles and market leader Telefonica del Peru "B" with 0.92 percent to 6.60 soles.

Among the losers were miner Morococha with 7.49 percent to 7.90 soles, cement-maker Cementos Lima with 1.69 percent to 58 soles, and industrial company Aceros Arequipa with 0.62 percent to 1.60 soles.
